> What to change on an existing Docker Compose deployment when moving from one release of `crisalid-deployment` to
> the next. One section per release, newest first. A fresh installation does not need this page: follow
> [Docker Compose - Step by Step](step-by-step.qmd).

# 1.6 → 1.7

## Component versions

| Component | 1.6 | 1.7 |
|---|---|---|
| `crisalid-ikg` | 1.6 | 1.7 |
| `crisalid-apollo` | 1.6 | 1.7 |
| `sovisuplus` | 1.6 | 1.7 |
| `crisalid-agents-chat-api` | 1.6 | 1.7 |
| `crisalid-agents-batch` (chat API image) | not deployed | 1.7 |
| `crisalid-agents-owui` (OpenWebUI pipelines) | 1.6 | **removed** |
| `crisalid-neo4j-mcp-toolbox` | 1.0 | 1.1 |
| OpenWebUI | 0.9.5 | 0.13.0 |
| OpenSearch for the Horizon Europe topic index | not deployed | 2.19.3 |
| CDB DAGs (`CDB_DAGS_REF`) | v1.1.0 | v1.2.0 |
| `svp-harvester`, `crisalid-vocab-search` | 1.6 | unchanged |
| `crisalid-org-registry`, `crisalid-taxi`, `svp-jel-proxy`, `crisalid-maintenance` | 1.0 | unchanged |

## What changes

**End-to-end authentication of the AI stack.** This is the breaking change of the release.

- The chat clients (the SoVisu+ assistant and OpenWebUI) no longer call the agents with a shared API key: they forward
  the Keycloak access token of the signed-in user.
- The chat API no longer queries the MCP toolbox with a service account. It validates the user's token (issuer,
  audience `crisalid-agents`, expiry), exchanges it for a token of audience `crisalid-graph-mcp` and queries the
  toolbox under the identity of the person, which the toolbox injects into the Cypher queries.
- There is no "internal" Keycloak host any more: every container uses the public Keycloak URL, which is the single
  issuer (`iss`) of the stack.
- The OpenWebUI pipelines server (`crisalid-agents-owui`, port 9099) is gone. A single service,
  `crisalid-agents-chat-api` (port 9100), serves every client: the NDJSON API used by SoVisu+ and an OpenAI-compatible
  API (chat completions) for OpenWebUI, which now sees the agents as models behind an OAuth connection instead of a
  pipeline behind an API key.

See [Crisalid AI → Security](../ai/security.qmd) and
[Keycloak → Clients & scopes](../security/keycloak/clients-scopes.qmd).

**New optional features**, each behind its own profile:

- [Horizon Europe topics](../ai/horizon-europe.qmd): the topic index (`horizon_europe_index` profile), the Horizon
  topic finder agent and the Topic-to-Researcher Match batch (`crisalid-agents-batch` service);
- [SorboBot](../ai/sorbobot.qmd), the research expertise agent, which relies on `crisalid-taxi`;
- a direct sign-in route for SoVisu+ (`SVP_KEYCLOAK_IDP_HINT`) and a switch for its assistant (`SVP_CHAT_ENABLED`).

## 1. Check out the release

```bash
git fetch --tags origin
git switch -c prod/1.7 v1.7.0
```

Do the next two steps (environment files, Keycloak) before restarting the stack.

## 2. Environment files

### `docker/.env` (shared)

Remove:

```env
KEYCLOAK_INTERNAL_HOST=…                 # no internal Keycloak host any more
SOVISUPLUS_KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_ID=…          # moved to sovisuplus/.env
SOVISUPLUS_KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_SECRET=…      # moved to sovisuplus/.env
CRISALID_AGENTS_PIPELINES_API_KEY=…      # no API key any more
SOVISUPLUS_CHAT_API_KEY=…                # no API key any more
```

Add:

```env
# OpenWebUI public URL (OAuth callback ${OPENWEBUI_URL}/oauth/oidc/callback, web origin)
OPENWEBUI_URL=https://<openwebui public host>

# Only when TLS ends at a reverse proxy in front of Keycloak: lets the containers reach the proxy
KEYCLOAK_NETWORK_ALIAS=keycloak.internal

# Only when KEYCLOAK_PORT is 443 or 80: Keycloak omits the default port in the iss claim
KEYCLOAK_ISSUER=https://<keycloak public host>/realms/<realm>
```

Change:

```env
# Which ref (tag/branch) to deploy for DAGs repo in prod
CDB_DAGS_REF=v1.2.0
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## Do not skip `CDB_DAGS_REF`
The `.env` of an existing deployment still holds the previous tag, and checking out the new release does not change
it. If it is left as is, `configure_cdb.sh prod` clones the old tag again and Airflow keeps running the previous
version of the DAGs code.
:::

`KEYCLOAK_SCHEME`, `KEYCLOAK_HOST`, `KEYCLOAK_PORT` and `KEYCLOAK_REALM` stay and must describe the **public** URL of
Keycloak. Leave `KEYCLOAK_NETWORK_ALIAS` unset when Keycloak itself answers on `KEYCLOAK_PORT` (local HTTP, or local
TLS with mkcert). The reasons behind both settings are explained in
[Keycloak issuer inside the stack](../ai/docker-compose.qmd#keycloak-issuer).

### `docker/sovisuplus/.env`

Add, with the values taken from the former `docker/.env`:

```env
SOVISUPLUS_KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_ID=sovisuplus
SOVISUPLUS_KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_SECRET=<secret of the sovisuplus client>

# Help button: 'url' opens SVP_HELP_URL, 'mail' mails SVP_MAINTENANCE_MAIL_ADDRESS. Unset = button hidden.
SVP_HELP_LINK_TYPE=url
```

`FIELD_ENC_PRIMARY_KID` and `FIELD_ENC_KEYS_JSON` already existed; they are now also used to encrypt the Keycloak
tokens of the sessions in the database, so make sure they hold real keys (`openssl rand -base64 32`).

Optional: `SVP_KEYCLOAK_IDP_HINT` (direct sign-in route `/transient-sso`) and `SVP_CHAT_ENABLED=false` (hides the
assistant; the `neo4j-mcp` and `crisalid-agents-chat-api` profiles can then be left out).

### `docker/openwebui/.env`

Remove:

```env
OPENWEBUI_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET=…      # replaced by OPENWEBUI_KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_SECRET
OPENWEBUI_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID=…          # now optional, defaults to open-webui (the client to create in Keycloak)
OPENWEBUI_OPENID_PROVIDER_URL=…      # now optional, defaults to the public Keycloak issuer of docker/.env
OPENWEBUI_OPENID_REDIRECT_URI=…      # now optional, defaults to ${OPENWEBUI_URL}/oauth/oidc/callback
```

Add:

```env
OPENWEBUI_KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_SECRET=<secret of the open-webui client>
# OpenWebUI >= 0.13: key encrypting the OAuth tokens kept in the server-side sessions
OPENWEBUI_OAUTH_SESSION_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY=<openssl rand -hex 32>
OPENWEBUI_ENABLE_OAUTH_SIGNUP=true   # if accounts are created at the first SSO login
```

### `docker/crisalid-agents/.env`

Add or update:

```env
# Agents loaded by the single chat API service
CRISALID_AGENTS_AGENTS=generic_agent,project_topic_matching,sorbobot

# New, mandatory outside local development: agents each Keycloak client (azp claim) may call
AGENT_ALLOW_LIST=sovisuplus:generic_agent,project_topic_matching;open-webui:generic_agent,project_topic_matching,sorbobot

CRISALID_AGENTS_KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_ID=crisalid-agents
CRISALID_AGENTS_KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_SECRET=<secret of the crisalid-agents client>
CRISALID_AGENTS_KEYCLOAK_SSL_VERIFY=true
```

A client absent from `AGENT_ALLOW_LIST` may call no agent: OpenWebUI then shows an empty model list and SoVisu+
receives `403 agent_not_allowed`. Only list in `CRISALID_AGENTS_AGENTS` the agents whose prerequisites are deployed:
`project_topic_matching` needs the Horizon Europe topic index, `sorbobot` needs `crisalid-taxi`.

Optional, leave them commented out unless needed: `CHAT_API_AUDIENCE` (`crisalid-agents`), `MIN_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS`
(`120`) and `MCP_AUDIENCE` (`crisalid-graph-mcp`, must be identical on the `neo4j-mcp` side). The other new variables
(`HORIZON_*`, `TRM_*`, `SORBOBOT_*`, `CRISALID_TAXI_URL`) have working defaults; see `.env.sample`.

### `docker/horizon-europe-index/.env` (new)

The file must exist even if the profile is never started, because the main compose file includes it:

```bash
cp docker/horizon-europe-index/.env.sample docker/horizon-europe-index/.env
```

### `docker/neo4j-mcp/.env`

Nothing to add. The toolbox reads `KEYCLOAK_*` from the shared `.env`, requires the audience `crisalid-graph-mcp` and
validates the tokens against the JWKS of the public issuer.

## 3. Keycloak

`configure_keycloak.sh` renders the realm template from `docker/.env` and the three service `.env` files, and Keycloak
imports it at startup. **On an existing realm the import changes nothing**: the configuration below has to be done by
hand in the admin console. The step-by-step procedure is on
[Clients & scopes → Manual configuration](../security/keycloak/clients-scopes.qmd#manual-configuration); in short:

- **`sovisuplus` client** (exists already): turn *Direct access grants* and *Service accounts roles* **off** (the 1.6
  realm template enabled them by mistake).
- **New clients**: `open-webui` (user login of OpenWebUI), `crisalid-graph-mcp` (no credentials, exists only to be
  named as an audience) and `crisalid-agents` (*Service accounts roles* and *Standard token exchange* on).
- **New client scopes**: `crisalid-agents-audience`, attached as *Default* to `sovisuplus` and `open-webui`, and
  `crisalid-graph-mcp-audience`, attached as *Default* to `crisalid-agents`.
- **Access token lifespan**: 15 minutes on `sovisuplus` and `open-webui`.

Copy the secret of each client into the `.env` file of its service (step 2), then run the checks of
[Clients & scopes → Verification](../security/keycloak/clients-scopes.qmd#verification).

## 4. Redeploy

From `docker/`, with your usual `-f` files and `--profile` options. The `crisalid-agents-owui` profile no longer
exists: remove it from your commands.

```bash
# DAGs of the directory bridge: check that it prints "Using DAGs repo ref: v1.2.0"
./configure_cdb.sh prod

docker compose -f docker-compose.yaml -f docker-compose.prod.yaml \
  --profile … pull --include-deps

# --remove-orphans deletes the former crisalid-agents-owui container
docker compose -f docker-compose.yaml -f docker-compose.prod.yaml \
  --profile … up -d --remove-orphans
```

`keycloak`, `neo4j-mcp`, `crisalid-agents-chat-api`, `sovisuplus` and `openwebui` are recreated because their image or
configuration changed. Check that Keycloak was: the network alias only takes effect on a new container.

From the SoVisu+ container (or any other), the public Keycloak hostname must resolve to the reverse proxy, not to a
Docker address, and the public OIDC endpoint must answer:

```bash
docker compose exec sovisuplus sh -c '
  getent hosts <keycloak public host>
  wget -qO- https://<keycloak public host>/realms/<realm>/.well-known/openid-configuration | head -c 200'
```

## 5. After the restart

### OpenWebUI: connection to the agents

In **Admin panel → Settings → Connections**, delete the former "pipelines" connection (`…:9099`, API key) and create
an OpenAI-compatible connection:

- **URL**: `http://crisalid-agents-chat-api:9100/v1`
- **Auth type**: **System OAuth** (no API key, *Forward cookies* off)

The models listed are the agents allowed to the `open-webui` client in `AGENT_ALLOW_LIST`. A user with a local account
that is not linked to the SSO gets no token: the model list is empty for them. Existing users have to sign in again so
that a server-side OAuth session exists. Details: [Configuring OpenWebUI](../ai/configuring-openwebui.qmd).

### SoVisu+

The existing sessions do not carry the Keycloak session identifier: users have to sign in again, otherwise the chat
widget answers `401 reauthentication_required` (the rest of the application keeps working).

### Optional: Horizon Europe topics

To use the Horizon topic finder or the Topic-to-Researcher Match, upload the work programme PDFs and build the index
as described in [Horizon Europe topics](../ai/horizon-europe.qmd).
